Congress seeks SC nod to pose 48 questions to EC, CEC Gyanesh Kumar over 'vote chori' 
 Edited by Priyanka Jaiswal / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Nov 16, 2026, 16:54 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium

 Print Congress seeks clarification on how many decisions taken by the CEC had been opposed by the other two Election Commissioners. NEW DELHI: The Congress on Monday said the Election Commission of India 's (ECI) affidavit before the Supreme Court had failed to address questions raised over alleged "Vote Chori", adding that INDIA bloc leaders now had sought the court's permission to submit an interrogatory to the poll body. In a post on X, the party said a list of 48 questions had been submitted for the Election Commission, including chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the two Election Commissioners and the Director General of IT, to answer over alleged lapses in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.  As per news agency PTI, Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi has also told the Supreme Court that the Election Commission's response failed to identify officials who authorised changes to the online version of Form 6 in connection with the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Gandhi and other petitioners have sought sworn replies from the Deputy Election Commissioner and other officials on who authorised the SIR, the exclusion of voters and the upgrades and alterations made to the Election Commission's online portal. The party has also sought clarification on how many decisions taken by the CEC had been opposed by the other two Election Commissioners. Congress alleged that lapses in the SIR exercise had paved the way for what it termed "Vote Chori" and called for the poll panel's top officials to personally respond to the questions.
